newsitem.title: POLAND: NBP CAPS ZLOTY RISE, REVREPO RAISES T/N RATES.
newsitem.headline: NBP CAPS ZLOTY RISE, REVREPO RAISES T/N RATES.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland gave the restive zloty a smack on Tuesday by buying some $30 million to confirm it did not want the Polish unit to firm above 2.5 percent from the floating parity rate, dealers said.

They said the zloty inched up at midday to 2.51 percent from the trading band centre, on the back of small-scale foreign T-bill purchases, even though the central bank has been pounding it at that level for the last three days.
"The zloty peeked just above 2.5 percent and immediately the NBP brought it down, showing that that level was to be respected," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.

The zloty closed at 3.1340/50 to the dollar, down from 3.1300/14 on Monday and at 1.8360/70 to the mark, down from 1.8365/71. It closed down at 2.41/2.37 percent from the trading band centre against Monday's 2.46/2.43 percent.
"The slight currency selling pressure might have come from some further T-bill buying by foreign investors, but it must have been small scale," one dealer said.

Dealers said the secondary T-bill market was dominated by domestic investors searching for longer-term paper as the bulk of the 600 million zloty offer of 52-week bills at Monday's primary tender has been bought by foreign investors.
But they said foreigners were also present, keen to buy zloty instruments now, when yields seem to have topped out, inflation prospects were good and the zloty relatively weak.

The shortest 8-week paper traded at 20.80/21.00 percent against the primary tender's average yield of 21.46 percent while the 52-week paper was at 21.30/21.15 percent against the primary tender's average yield of 21.68 percent.

On the money market overnight rates closed at 18.00/21.00 percent, up from 12.00/20.00 percent at opening lifted by a 571 million zloty sale of 91-day NBP-bills with overnight value date. Their average yield eased to 22.13 percent from 22.19.
Tomorrow/next rates were likewise brought up to 20.50/21.20 percent by a 1.8 billion zloty reverse repo with a tomorrow/next value date, which had an unchanged maximum accepted rate of 22.15 percent.
Both O/N and T/N cash were seen trading back above 21.00 percent on Wednesday.
